gaps.concept: GHRH stimulates GH; CRH stimulates ACTH; TRH stimulates TSH; pulsatile GnRH stimulates LH and FSH.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks which hypothalamic signal controls a deficient anterior pituitary hormone.

gaps.concept: Continuous GnRH exposure desensitizes pituitary GnRH receptors and suppresses LH and FSH; pulsatile exposure stimulates them.
gaps.why_tested: A GnRH agonist produces opposite gonadotropin responses depending on how it is delivered.

gaps.concept: Pituitary stalk compression interrupts dopamine delivery, raising prolactin while reducing other anterior pituitary hormones.
gaps.why_tested: A sellar mass causes hyperprolactinemia alongside deficiencies of other pituitary hormones.

gaps.concept: Low target-gland hormone with elevated tropic hormone indicates primary failure; low or inappropriately normal tropic hormone indicates central failure.
gaps.why_tested: Paired hormone measurements must localize a defect to the target gland or hypothalamic–pituitary axis.

gaps.concept: In central hypothyroidism, free T4 is low while TSH may be low or inappropriately normal.
gaps.why_tested: A normal-range TSH accompanies low free T4 in a patient with a pituitary lesion.

gaps.concept: Inhibin from gonadal supporting cells selectively suppresses pituitary FSH secretion.
gaps.why_tested: A question asks which gonadotropin changes when inhibin falls.

gaps.concept: Prolactin drives milk production; oxytocin contracts mammary myoepithelial cells to eject milk.
gaps.why_tested: A postpartum vignette distinguishes absent milk synthesis from failure of milk letdown.

gaps.concept: Nipple stimulation increases prolactin and oxytocin release; cervical stretch triggers oxytocin-mediated positive feedback during labor.
gaps.why_tested: A reflex or hormone question links suckling or cervical stretch to pituitary secretion.

gaps.concept: Posterior pituitary histology shows pituicytes and Herring bodies, axonal swellings containing stored ADH or oxytocin.
gaps.why_tested: A histology image asks for the posterior lobe or its hormone-storage structures.

gaps.concept: Anterior pituitary chromophobes stain poorly and often represent degranulated hormone-secreting cells.
gaps.why_tested: A pituitary section asks the identity of pale cells among acidophils and basophils.

gaps.concept: The anterior pituitary relies chiefly on portal blood; the posterior pituitary has a direct arterial supply.
gaps.why_tested: A vascular injury preferentially impairs anterior pituitary function while sparing posterior secretion.

gaps.concept: The cavernous sinuses border the pituitary laterally and contain cranial nerves III, IV, V1, V2, and VI.
gaps.why_tested: A laterally expanding sellar mass causes diplopia or facial sensory loss in addition to endocrine findings.

gaps.concept: Rising plasma osmolality stimulates ADH release; substantial volume or pressure loss also stimulates release.
gaps.why_tested: A dehydration or hemorrhage vignette asks which posterior pituitary hormone changes.

gaps.concept: GH and prolactin signal through JAK–STAT receptors; GH also promotes lipolysis and opposes insulin action.
gaps.why_tested: A receptor-pathway or hyperglycemia question asks for a direct effect of a pituitary hormone.

gaps.concept: TSH, LH, and FSH are glycoproteins sharing an alpha subunit; their distinct beta subunits confer specificity.
gaps.why_tested: A hormone-structure question asks which pituitary hormones share a subunit.

gaps.concept: Dopamine D2 antagonists, including antipsychotics and metoclopramide, can cause hyperprolactinemia; D2 agonists suppress prolactin.
gaps.why_tested: A medication-associated galactorrhea vignette asks for the receptor mechanism.

gaps.concept: Primary hypothyroidism can raise TRH and thereby raise prolactin, causing galactorrhea or menstrual disturbance.
gaps.why_tested: High TSH and prolactin occur together without a prolactin-secreting tumor.

gaps.concept: GnRH neurons migrate from the olfactory placode; failed migration causes Kallmann syndrome with anosmia and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with delayed puberty and impaired smell has low LH and FSH.

gaps.concept: POU1F1 (PIT1) defects impair somatotrophs, lactotrophs, and thyrotrophs, causing combined GH, prolactin, and TSH deficiency.
gaps.why_tested: A child has growth failure and central hypothyroidism with preserved ACTH and gonadotropins.

gaps.concept: Craniopharyngioma arises from Rathke pouch remnants and classically appears as a calcified, cystic suprasellar mass in a child.
gaps.why_tested: A child with growth failure and visual symptoms has a calcified suprasellar lesion.
